lessons.title: Χαιρετισμοί & Γνωριμία (Greetings & Introductions)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Formal & informal greetings, polite addresses, personal pronouns, and core verbs (είμαι, λέω, γράφω).
lessons.lesson_notes:
Unit 1 Core Grammar Notes:
• Vocative Singular: Masculine nouns in -ος end in -ε (κύριε Παπαδόπουλε). Feminine nouns in -α/-η remain unchanged (κυρία, δεσποινίς).
• Copular Verb 'είμαι' (Present): εγώ είμαι, εσύ είσαι, αυτός/αυτή/αυτό είναι, εμείς είμαστε, εσείς είστε, αυτοί/αυτές/αυτά είναι.
• Stating Names: 'Με λένε + Accusative' (e.g. Με λένε Κώστα) or 'Είμαι ο/η + Nominative'.

entries.notes: Vocative singular drops final -ς and changes to -ε (κύριε).
entries.keg_communicative_function: Addressing individuals politely and formal introductions

entries.notes: Vocative singular is identical to nominative: κυρία.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Addressing adult women respectfully

entries.notes: In daily spoken Greek, often truncated to the vocative particle 'δεσποινίς'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Polite address to an unmarried young woman

entries.notes: Neuter noun in -μα; plural adds -τα (τα ονόματα). Takes a second accent before possessive clitic: το όνομά μου.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for and stating names in introductions

entries.notes: Proparoxytone noun (accent on antepenult). Takes an enclitic accent before possessive: το επώνυμό μου.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Official registration and identity forms

entries.notes: Neuter noun in -μα (plural: τα γράμματα). Essential for KEG listening task on name spelling.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Spelling Greek names and asking about the alphabet

entries.notes: Vocative singular: (ε) φίλε μου! Note masculine nominative article 'ο'.
entries.example_el: Αυτός είναι ο φίλος μου, ο Νίκος.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Introducing social acquaintances and friends

entries.notes: Regular feminine in -η with plural in -ες. Accusative drops final -ν before fricatives (τη φίλη).
entries.example_el: Αυτή είναι η φίλη μου, η Μαρία.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Introducing female friends

entries.notes: Copular auxiliary verb. Full present paradigm: είμαι, είσαι, είναι, είμαστε, είστε (είσαστε), είναι.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Self-identification, stating profession and identity

entries.english: to say / to tell / to call
entries.notes: 'Με λένε + Accusative' literally means 'They call me'. Most natural everyday way to state your name.
entries.example_el: Με λένε Κώστα και είμαι μαθητής.
entries.example_en: My name is Kostas and I am a student.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating one's name via direct object formula ('με λένε')

entries.notes: Model Type A regular active verb (-ω, -εις, -ει, -ουμε, -ετε, -ουν).
entries.example_en: How do you write (spell) your name?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking how names and contact information are spelled

entries.notes: Modern Greek is a pro-drop language; 'εγώ' is reserved for emphasis or contrast.
entries.example_el: Εγώ είμαι από την Ελλάδα, εσύ;
entries.example_en: I am from Greece, and you?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Emphasizing personal identity or contrasting with others

entries.notes: Informal address. Contrasts strictly with the formal polite 'εσείς'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Directly addressing a friend, colleague, or child

entries.notes: Functions both as 3rd person subject pronoun ('he') and demonstrative ('this').
entries.keg_communicative_function: Introducing and pointing out a male individual

entries.notes: Feminine nominative singular. Plural is 'αυτές'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Introducing and pointing out a female individual

entries.notes: Neuter singular. Universal question prompt in KEG A1 listening items: 'Τι είναι αυτό;'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about or identifying objects and concepts

entries.notes: Triggers 1st person plural verb ending -ουμε / -μαστε.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing shared identity or group actions

entries.notes: The plural of courtesy (πληθυντικός ευγενείας). Essential KEG A1 social competence marker.
entries.example_en: Where are you from? (formal or plural)
entries.keg_communicative_function: Polite formula for addressing adult strangers or a group

entries.notes: Gender agreement is mandatory in 3rd person plural: άντρες -> αυτοί, γυναίκες -> αυτές, πράγματα -> αυτά.
entries.example_el: Αυτοί είναι οι νέοι συμμαθητές μας.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying multiple third persons or objects

entries.notes: Always takes a written accent (τόνος) in questions to distinguish from the conjunction 'πως' (that).
entries.example_en: What is your name? (Literally: How do they call you?)
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about well-being, names, and methods

entries.notes: Always accented. Agrees in gender with the referenced noun: ποιος είναι αυτός; / ποια είναι αυτή;.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about the identity of specific persons or objects

entries.notes: Monosyllabic and never accented. 'Τι κάνεις;' is the ubiquitous everyday Greek greeting.
entries.example_en: How are you doing? / What are you doing?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for information about things, actions, and states

entries.notes: Derived from 'υγεία σου' (to your health). Used symmetrically for both 'hello' and 'goodbye'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Greeting or saying farewell to friends, family, and peers

entries.notes: Standard formal opening for KEG oral examination interviews.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Greeting professionals, elders, strangers, or multiple people

entries.notes: Compound of καλή + μέρα. Written as a single word with accent on -ε-.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Standard daytime greeting from dawn until early afternoon

entries.notes: Used exclusively as a greeting upon arrival/meeting, never as a farewell.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Greeting upon arrival from mid-afternoon onward

entries.notes: Strictly a parting farewell before sleep; never used as a greeting upon arrival.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Wishing someone a good night when taking leave or sleeping

entries.notes: Often paired with 'σας' in polite social contexts: Αντίο σας.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Formal or standard farewell when departing

entries.notes: Literally: 'We say them'. The most frequent casual goodbye in modern Greece.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Informal parting formula between friends and colleagues

entries.notes: Diphthong 'ευ' is pronounced as /ef/ before voiceless 'χ'. Often emphasized as 'ευχαριστώ πολύ'.
entries.example_en: Thank you very much for the help.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing gratitude politely

entries.notes: Two-way usage: 'please' when ordering/asking, and 'you are welcome' after 'ευχαριστώ'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Polite requests and responding to thanks

entries.notes: Spelled with double γ (γγ pronounced as velar nasal [ŋ]).
entries.example_en: Excuse me, who is the professor?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Apologizing or politely getting someone's attention

entries.english: pleased to meet you / nice to meet you
entries.notes: Standard social formula taught formulaically at A1 upon hearing someone's name.
entries.example_el: — Είμαι ο Γιάννης. — Χάρηκα, είμαι η Σοφία.
entries.example_en: — I am Giannis. — Pleased to meet you, I am Sofia.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Acknowledging an introduction politely

entries.notes: Adverbial form (πολύ). Must not be confused with the inflected adjective 'πολύς'.
entries.example_en: I am very well, thank you.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Modifying adjectives, adverbs, and verbs to express high degree

entries.notes: Adverb formed from the neuter plural of the adjective 'καλός'.
entries.example_en: — How are you? — Fine, and you?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating positive personal condition in greeting exchanges

lessons.title: Καταγωγή, Εθνικότητες & Γλώσσες (Origins, Nationalities & Languages)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Countries, nationalities, spoken languages, and verbs of residence & communication (μένω, μιλάω, μαθαίνω).
lessons.lesson_notes:
Unit 2 Core Grammar Notes:
• Expressing Origin: 'από + Accusative' (e.g., Από πού είσαι; — Είμαι από την Ελλάδα).
• Expressing Residence: 'σε + Accusative' contracts with article: σε + την = στην, σε + το = στο, σε + τον = στον (e.g., Μένω στην Αθήνα).
• Nationalities: Masculine in -ος/-ας/-ης, Feminine in -ίδα/-α (ο Έλληνας / η Ελληνίδα, ο Άγγλος / η Αγγλίδα).
• Languages: Neuter plural with definite article (τα ελληνικά, τα αγγλικά, τα γαλλικά).

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -α with plural in -ες. Note: 'η Χώρα' on Greek islands also refers to the main town.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for and stating geographic origins

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -η ending in -εις in nominative plural (οι πόλεις).
entries.example_el: Η Αθήνα είναι μία μεγάλη πόλη.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating one's city of residence or origin

entries.notes: Ancient-declension neuter in -ος with plural in -η (τα κράτη).
entries.example_el: Η Ελλάδα είναι κράτος της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης.
entries.example_en: Greece is a member state of the European Union.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to geopolitical states in official contexts

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -ότητα (plural in -ότητες). Essential keyword in KEG reading forms.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Completing official registration cards and forms

entries.notes: Commonly paired with 'έχω' + adjective of nationality in the feminine.
entries.example_el: Έχω ελληνική καταγωγή αλλά μένω στον Καναδά.
entries.example_en: I have Greek heritage but I live in Canada.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Discussing ancestral background and cultural roots

entries.notes: Regular feminine in -α with plural in -ες. Root of English 'linguistics/glossary'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about linguistic competencies

entries.notes: Adjective 'μητρικός' (maternal) agrees with 'γλώσσα' in feminine nominative.
entries.example_el: Η μητρική μου γλώσσα είναι τα αγγλικά.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying one's primary native language

entries.notes: Takes final -ν in the accusative article before vowels: 'στην Ελλάδα', 'από την Ελλάδα'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Naming the target host country

entries.notes: Feminine proper noun. Accusative: την Αγγλία (keeps -ν before vowel).
entries.example_el: Ο φίλος μου είναι από την Αγγλία.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying country of origin

entries.notes: Crucial grammatical trap: feminine gender despite ending in -ος (accusative: την Κύπρο).
entries.example_el: Η Κύπρος είναι ένα όμορφο νησί.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Naming Greek-speaking countries and regions

entries.notes: Accusative drops -ν before γ: 'από τη Γαλλία', 'στη Γαλλία'.
entries.example_el: Η καθηγήτρια είναι από τη Γαλλία.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying European origin

entries.notes: Accusative drops -ν before γ: 'στη Γερμανία'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying European origin

entries.notes: Accusative retains -ν before vowel: 'στην Ιταλία'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying Mediterranean origin

entries.notes: Accusative retains -ν before vowel: 'από την Ισπανία'.
entries.example_el: Η Μαρία είναι από την Ισπανία.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying country of origin

entries.notes: Plural agreement: 'από τις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες', 'στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες'.
entries.example_el: Είμαι από τις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες της Αμερικής.
entries.example_en: I am from the United States of America.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying North American origin

entries.notes: Accusative retains -ν before vowel: 'στην Αυστραλία'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying country of origin and Greek diaspora center

entries.notes: Masculine noun in -ας; nominative plural is 'οι Έλληνες'.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating male Greek nationality

entries.notes: Feminine nationality suffix -ίδα with plural in -ίδες.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating female Greek nationality

entries.notes: Capitalized when denoting the national noun.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating male English nationality

entries.notes: Feminine nationality noun in -ίδα.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating female English nationality

entries.notes: Regular masculine in -ος (plural: οι Γάλλοι).
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating male French nationality

entries.notes: Feminine nationality form in -ίδα.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating female French nationality

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine (accent on final syllable -ός).
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating male German nationality

entries.notes: Feminine nationality form in -ίδα.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating female German nationality

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine noun in -ός.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating male Italian nationality

entries.notes: Feminine counterpart of ο Ιταλός.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating female Italian nationality

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine noun in -ός.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating male Spanish nationality

entries.notes: Feminine counterpart of ο Ισπανός.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating female Spanish nationality

entries.notes: Adjectives in Greek are written in lower case (ελληνικός) unlike the proper national nouns (ο Έλληνας).
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing objects, concepts, and traditions related to Greece

entries.notes: Language names in Modern Greek are grammatically neuter plural adjectives (τα ελληνικά).
entries.example_en: I am learning Greek at the university.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to the Greek language as a field of study or speech

entries.notes: Neuter plural without capital letter when denoting language.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to the English language

entries.notes: Neuter plural language designation.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to the French language

entries.english: to live / to reside / to stay
entries.notes: Type A active verb. Governs 'σε + Accusative' for location (μένω στο Παρίσι, μένω στη Ρώμη).
entries.example_el: Μένω στην Αθήνα, στην οδό Πανεπιστημίου.
entries.example_en: I live in Athens, on Panepistimiou Street.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating address, neighborhood, city, or country of residence

entries.notes: Archetypal Type B1 contracted active verb (-άω/-ώ, -άς, -άει/-ά, -άμε, -άτε, -άνε/-ούν).
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing language skills and conversational communication

entries.notes: Type A active verb with stem ending in -αιν- (-αίνω, -αίνεις, -αίνει).
entries.example_en: We are learning Modern Greek at school.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about learning languages and subjects

entries.notes: Crucial survival phrase for KEG oral examination. Conjugates like μαθαίνω.
entries.example_el: Δεν καταλαβαίνω, παρακαλώ μιλάτε πιο αργά.
entries.example_en: I do not understand, please speak more slowly.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing comprehension or requesting clarification

entries.notes: Type A active verb. Frequently used in questions with polite 'εσείς' (ξέρετε).
entries.example_en: Do you know where the school is?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating knowledge of facts, information, or languages

entries.notes: Always governs the Accusative case: από + τον/την/το/τους/τις/τα.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing origin, provenance, and nationality background

entries.notes: Contracted systematically with the definite article (στο, στη, στον, στα, στις, στους).
entries.example_el: Ζω στην Αθήνα και δουλεύω στο κέντρο.
entries.example_en: I live in Athens and work in the centre.

grammatical_info.contractions: σε + τον = στον, σε + την = στη(ν), σε + το = στο, σε + τους = στους, σε + τις = στις, σε + τα = στα

entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing location and residence

entries.notes: Adverbial modifier. Often contrasted with 'πολύ' (very / a lot).
entries.example_en: I speak only a little Greek.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing basic or emerging language competency
